newsitem.title: USA: Two Miss. men sentenced for extermination binge.
newsitem.headline: Two Miss. men sentenced for extermination binge.

text.p: Two men were sentenced to lengthy federal prison terms for spraying scores of private homes with a deadly pesticide normally used by cotton farmers, court officials said Tuesday.

Paul Walls, 62, and Dock Eatman, 64, were acting as unlicensed exterminators when they treated homes near Mississippi's Gulf Coast with the insecticide known as methyl parathion. A teaspoonful of the chemical can be fatal, but the Environmental Protection Agency allows its use outdoors where sunlight renders it harmless.

Walls and Eatman sprayed the poison inside hundreds of homes in Jackson County, authorities said. The contaminated properties included Eatman's own house as well as those of his children and his mother-in-law.

They were convicted this year in separate jury trials. On Monday U.S. Magistrate Louis Guirola sentenced Walls to 78 months for spraying 48 buildings with the chemical. Eatman received a 63-month sentence for spraying 21 buildings.
The pair also face a year of supervised probation following their prison terms. They remained free on bond pending a ruling by the 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in New Orleans.

Walls, who is partially deaf and has little education, received the maximum sentence for a federal misdemeanor partly because he continued to spray the deadly chemical after being ordered to stop by a local court in June 1996.
Eatman, who filed for bankruptcy, begged the federal magistrate for mercy before his sentence was imposed.

"I did not know that this stuff was like they said it was," he was quoted as saying by the Biloxi Sun Herald. "I got it in my own mouth and my eyes and I washed it out with olive oil and it never hurt or killed me or any of my family."
